summary: Well-executed, artifact-rich preregistered paired evaluation of a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline versus LLM-only generation for intent-to-configuration NetOps tasks. Study provides strong reproducibility evidence (extensive artifact/hashes, Dockerized harness, deterministic validator). The confirmatory outcome is null because the baseline already satisfied the validator on every task (200/200), largely arising from the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (single LLM candidate evaluated under both arms) and task/validator scope. The manuscript documents limitations and publishes full artifacts, but requires targeted clarifications and minor corrections to reconcile analysis reporting and to make the limiting design choices and their consequences explicit and unambiguous.
critical_issues: Key inferential limitation from preregistered 'shared_initial_candidate' semantics: using a single LLM candidate per task for both arms removes the opportunity for repairs to produce different guarded outcomes; this design choice materially reduces the experiment's ability to test the intended intervention and must be made unmistakably explicit in the Abstract, Introduction (final research question), Methods, Results, and Disclosure as a core limitation rather than an incidental detail.

Inconsistency between analysis artifacts and manuscript reporting about the primary statistical test(s): analysis records include both an exact McNemar label and references to the preregistered Wilcoxon signed-rank test; the manuscript reports a Wilcoxon p-value but the confirmatory_results.test field names McNemar. This discrepancy must be reconciled, justified, and disclosed as either (a) a post-hoc additional test or (b) a reporting error, with exact test outputs and artifact references provided.

Missing explicit reporting of repair/iteration activity: the paper states no repairs were invoked indirectly (identical response hashes), but does not provide a concise quantitative statement or table showing the number of repair attempts and iteration counts (per preregistration exploratory questions). The absence of any repair invocation is central to interpreting the null result and must be explicitly reported with artifact pointers (scoring/provider/manifest entries).
required_revisions: Add an explicit, prominent statement in the Abstract and at the end of the Introduction that the preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false) was used and that this semantics causes a single LLM-produced candidate to be evaluated under both baseline and guarded arms—explain succinctly that when no repairs are invoked this makes the two arms identical and limits the confirmatory inference. Cite the preregistration and the execution_manifest artifact (provide SHA-256 entries already present).

In Methods and Results, report the repair-invocation statistics exactly (resolvable from provided artifacts): number of tasks where a repair attempt was executed, distribution of repair-iteration counts (median, IQR, or explicit zero if none), and pointer to the execution/provider_calls, scoring JSONs, or transformation manifest entries that show zero repair calls (e.g., execution/provider_calls/* and execution/scoring/*). If repair attempts = 0 for all confirmatory tasks, state this plainly and include two representative task hashes (e.g., task-000001 and task-000002) to illustrate identical baseline/guarded responses and link to the stored response hashes in the execution_manifest.

Resolve and disclose the statistical-test naming/usage inconsistency: (a) inspect the analysis log artifacts to confirm which tests were executed (Wilcoxon signed-rank per preregistration and any additional exact McNemar or other tests); (b) update the manuscript to identify the preregistered primary test (Wilcoxon) and report its exact statistic and p-value from the archived analysis artifacts; (c) if an additional test (McNemar or others) was run, label it explicitly as an additional check and report its result and the artifact path; (d) add a short deviations-from-preregistration note stating whether any test beyond the preregistered Wilcoxon was executed and why. Provide exact artifact references (analysis/results.json, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, or relevant CSVs) to support the corrected reporting.

Clarify model-call accounting and stopping-rule/episode-count reporting: explicitly state why model_calls_used = 200 while planned_episode_count = 400 (i.e., preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1 produced one model call per task evaluated in both arms). Update the Methods and Disclosure text to make this accounting explicit and point readers to the execution manifest entries (model_calls_used, planned_episode_count, completed_episode_count).

Add a short, clearly labeled Results subsection/table that lists the confirmatory contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00), the paired estimate, bootstrap CI, exact p-value(s), and direct pointers to the analysis artifact files used to compute them (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). This ensures claims are directly traceable to the archived artifacts without requiring new computation.
optional_revisions: Consider adding a one-paragraph explanatory example (single task) in an appendix-style boxed example within the five pages showing the input intent, the shared LLM candidate, the validator checks, and the identical baseline/guarded response hash and score (use task-000001 or another representative task).

Report both the preregistered Wilcoxon and exact McNemar tests (if both were computed) in a small combined statistics table to aid readers who expect contingency-based tests for paired binary outcomes.

Briefly expand the Discussion with an explicit recommended experimental design checklist for future work (e.g., prefer independent-condition-generation for confirmatory tests of repair loops; pre-specify repair-triggering conditions; increase model diversity), citing that these follow directly from the observed artifact-backed null outcome.

Include a short, explicit note in the Disclosure Statement that no post-lock manual edits were made to the reported analysis artifacts and point to the hash manifest entries used to verify the final manuscript numbers.
